title: Multichannel status orchestrator and translated templates
author: Lauren Chen
body:
Summary

This document defines the Multichannel Status Orchestrator pattern and provides a catalog of pre-approved, translated status templates for use on the Redwood status page, email, SMS, and account-level in-product notices. It standardizes sequencing, severity mapping, escalation ownership, and localization to ensure fast, consistent, brand-safe communications during operational incidents.

Audience
- On-call SREs and ops bridge leads
- Customer Success (CS) incident liaisons
- Legal and PR for high-severity incidents
- Product and platform owners responsible for downstream status updates

Scope and goals
- Cover: status page messages, customer emails, SMS alerts, in-console banners, and partner notifications.
- Goals: speed (first public notice <= 10 min for Sev1/S3P), tone consistency, accurate scope, and multilingual coverage for EN/ES/FR (priority) + fallback guidance for other languages.

When to use this orchestrator
1) Any incident with customer-facing impact (latency, errors, throttling, model quality) that meets our customer-impact tiers.
2) Planned maintenance affecting customers for >15 minutes.
3) When a single channel update (status page only) is insufficient — use multichannel for incidents hitting enterprise customers or when SLO crediting is possible.

Ownership and run ownership model
- Primary owner: Incident Bridge Lead (typically on-call SRE).
- Secondary owner (communication execution): On-call CS liaison.
- Legal/PR consulted for Sev1 external statements.
- Template maintenance: CS content guild; updates every quarter or after each major incident.

Severity mapping and timing commitments
| Severity | Redwood label | First public update target | Follow-up cadence | Channels to use |
|---|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| Sev1 / P0 | outage (critical customer impact) | <= 10 minutes | 30 min until stable, then hourly | Status page + Email + SMS + In-console banner + Slack enterprise channel |
| Sev2 / P1 | partial outage / high error rate | <= 30 minutes | 1 hour | Status page + Email + In-console banner |
| Sev3 / P2 | degraded latency/quality | <= 60 minutes | 4 hours | Status page + In-console banner |
| Maintenance | scheduled maintenance | 72 hours notice + reminder 2 hours prior | N/A | Status page + Email for affected customers |

Runbook: step-by-step communications workflow (bridge lead)
1. Confirm impact and scope with service owner (who does what, which customers affected).
2. Classify severity using the incident severity decision ladder (see related runbook).
3. Prepare first-public-message using the Short Notice template (English).
4. Post to Status Page (see API example below) and create an update draft for CS email/SMS channels.
5. Assign CS liaison to send targeted emails to enterprise tenants (copy includes timeline and mitigation).
6. If multilingual is required (see language matrix below), trigger translation pipeline (CS guild) and include translated messages in next update.
7. Schedule and post regular updates per the cadence. Ensure every update includes: what changed, current impact, mitigation steps, customer action (if any), ETA or next update window, and link to the status page.
8. Close the incident with a final summary (postmortem anchor) and publish a follow-up message containing root cause (when available) and remediation/fixes.

Status page API example (curl)
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"service":"inference-api","impact":"partial_outage","title":"Elevated 5xx errors affecting text-generation","body":"We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting text generation requests. Tokenization paths are being validated. More details will follow.","severity":"high" }'

Template catalog: Short Notice (English)
- Title: "Investigating elevated errors affecting [service]"
- Body (first public): "We are currently investigating elevated errors affecting [service]. Some requests may fail with 5xx responses or experience increased latency. Engineers are actively investigating. We will post an update by [time window]."
- Actions for customers: "No action required right now. If you see persistent failures, contact support with request IDs."

Template catalog: Escalated Notice (English)
- Title: "Partial outage impacting [feature] — mitigation in progress"
- Body (follow-up): "We have identified a regression in [component]. A mitigation (fallback to model vX) is rolling out. Impact is reduced for most customers but persists for a subset. Estimated time to mitigation: ~ [ETA]."

Multilingual translated templates (examples)
- Spanish (ES):
  - Title: "Investigando errores elevados que afectan a [service]"
  - Body: "Actualmente estamos investigando errores elevados que afectan a [service]. Algunas solicitudes pueden fallar con respuestas 5xx o experimentar mayor latencia. Los ingenieros están investigando activamente. Publicaremos una actualización antes de [time window]."
- French (FR):
  - Title: "Investigation d'erreurs élevées affectant [service]"
  - Body: "Nous enquêtons actuellement sur des erreurs élevées affectant [service]. Certaines requêtes peuvent échouer avec des 5xx ou subir une latence accrue. Les ingénieurs enquêtent activement. Nous publierons une mise à jour avant [time window]."

Language matrix and precedence rules
- Priority locales: en-US (default), es-ES, fr-FR. For enterprise customers with tenant locale preference: use tenant locale if available.
- If a translation is not available within the first update window, post English with a short apology line: "Localized message forthcoming — English update provided below."

Channel-specific formatting notes
- SMS: keep <= 320 characters; include link to status page and support contact.
- Email: include incident ID, impact table (affected regions/tenants), and recommended mitigations for customers. Use the Email Notice template.
- In-console banner: include short call-to-action (CTA) and link to status page. Do not include internal debugging details.

Email Notice template (example)
Subject: "[Incident ID] — Impact to [service] (updates every 30m)"
Body:
Hello [Customer name],

We want to let you know that you may experience [brief impact description]. Our engineering teams are actively investigating and we will provide updates every [cadence].

What we know: [bullet list of affected regions / endpoints / tenant subsets]
What we're doing: [bullet list of mitigation steps]
If you need immediate assistance: contact support@redwood.ai with Incident ID [incident id].

Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Incident Team

Customer tiers and communication escalation matrix
| Customer tier | Channel | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise (contracted) | Email + Phone + Status page + Account PM | CS Liaison + Bridge Lead |
| Self-serve paying | Status page + Email | Bridge Lead + CS Broadcast |
| Free / trial | Status page | Bridge Lead |

Translation pipeline and turnaround SLA
- Rapid translation SLA for priority locales: 20 minutes for short notices (<=120 words) via CS guild rotation.
- Non-priority locale request: create ticket to Content Ops for 24–72 hour translation turnaround.
- If machine translation is used for immediate needs, the message must be labeled: "Machine translation — human review pending."

Templates for legal / PR review
- Use the Legal Review short-form: include impact facts, customer exposure (yes/no), and whether data loss is suspected. Submit PR/Legal at legal@redwood.ai with subject line: "LEGAL REVIEW REQUEST — Incident [ID]".

Post-incident cadence and postmortem inclusion
- Final customer-facing post: publish "Incident resolved" update within 24 hours with a summary and link to the postmortem.
- Postmortem must contain a customer-facing executive summary (2–3 paragraphs) and a technical appendix. CS authors the customer-facing summary.

Example status messages (full templates)
- SMS (short): "[INCIDENT ID] We are investigating elevated errors in [service]. Details: [short url to status]."
- In-console banner: "We are currently experiencing degraded [service]. See status.redwood.ai for updates."

Triage checklist for translation decisions (bridge lead)
1. Confirm affected customer list and locale preferences.
2. If >5 enterprise customers in same locale are affected -> require human translation.
3. Else: post English + note about localization.
4. Trigger CS guild if human translation required.

Governance and quality control
- Quarterly audit: sample 10 incidents and validate message timeliness, localization correctness, and adherence to templates.
- Incident communications training: mandatory for bridge leads and CS liaisons (1x per quarter).
- Template change process: propose PR in the content repo, two reviewers required (CS lead + SRE comms owner).

Appendix A — Example incident lifecycle timeline (Sev1)
- T+0m: Detection, bridge stood up, impact confirmed.
- T+5m: First public status page post (short notice).
- T+10m: Targeted enterprise email drafted and approved.
- T+30m: Mitigation rolling for subset; status page update + SMS to contracting customers.
- T+120m: Stabilized for 95% of traffic; hourly updates continue.
- T+24h: Incident closed, final summary posted, postmortem assigned.

Appendix B — Sample status page payload (JSON)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-20260208-1234",
  "service": "inference-api",
  "severity": "high",
  "title": "Investigating elevated 5xxs for text-generation",
  "body": "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting text-generation. More details to follow."
}

Appendix C — Contacts and escalation list
- On-call Bridge Lead: pager (primary on-call)
- CS Liaison: cs-oncall@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- PR: pr@redwood.ai
